builds_on.code: src/exit_rules_study.py (imported unchanged: loader, trades, rule_exit, rule_stats, mean_pct, share, cluster_t)

definitions.card: two contracts at one ask; result = average of the two = % of total entry cost; both: -30% stop; contract 1: +50% target, 60m clock (identical to the study's 30/50/60 cell); contract 2: after target 1 stop moves to entry, exits at +100%, its stop, or the 60m clock (from entry); every exit at the bid of the snapshot where it triggers; same-snapshot triggers share one bid

runner_rules.runner_a: Runner Card: -30% stop, sell half +50%, runner to +100%, breakeven stop after target 1, 60m clock
runner_rules.runner_b: (b) as the Runner Card but the runner target is +150%
runner_rules.runner_c: (c) after target 1 a 25% trailing stop from the peak bid replaces the breakeven stop; +100% target and 60m clock stay
runner_rules.runner_c_nocap: (c, other reading) 25% trailing stop after target 1, NO fixed profit target, capped by the 60m clock only

sell_first_25.label: sell at the first +25% (no loss line, 60m fallback)

definitions.intervals: 90% session-bootstrap of the mean, 2000 draws, rng seeded [20261011, group, rule, reading]; t = the study's cluster-robust t by session
definitions.vs_card: paired per-trade difference (runner total - card result); exactly 0 where target 1 never fills

calm_window_from_the_study.source: settled daily closes, close to close

reproduction.note: the comparison cells' numbers in 'comparison' are the study JSON's own; the recompute exists for the interval and the paired differences

looks.note: the brief named three rules (a, b, c); c was ambiguous (does the +100% target survive the trailing stop?) so both readings are run and counted: the brief's three rules alone would be 3 x 6 = 18 cells + 18 paired differences = 36 looks. The runner-stage decomposition and the comparison cells (re-read from the study) are not counted as new looks.
